### 2026-11-03: ### Schematic mostly done

**1.7h**

### Schematic mostly done

Okay, so I worked a bunch today in the morning. I got most of the schematic done. And I definitely wanted battery support because a lot of my projects I don't like using batteries for them.

And this was a little hard because there wasn't any clear instructions. But I was able to find some reference sources on the Raspberry Pi Pico data sheet. So I implemented that.

And putting the labels on everything took so long because there were like 40 labels that typed out and it was just really repetitive and really boring. But other than that, I think it was relatively straightforward.

I think I learned a bit about how it all works. So I'm pretty happy with what I did today.

### 2026-11-05: ### Schematic and PCB

**1.5h**

### Schematic and PCB

What I did today was I finished the schematic, which I have to double check my connections and run analysis on it, so everything works fine. I added three LEDs to it because I think that would be really cool, especially when I'm debugging, or just a little status display on what the microcontroller is doing. Okay, because we had a few extra pins. I'm going to leave a few pins empty for the actual microcontroller because there's no thing to really connect to them, so it doesn't really matter. Then I finished the schematic. Everything looks good. Continued following the guide and started throwing everything on the actual PCB. Based on the progress so far, it's very messy. There's a lot of things just all grouped up, and the labels really are just making everything worse. But I believe I can probably finish this in two, three days.
